hints: Look closely at W around 0.17 s where the solid ventricle line dips just below then shoots above the dotted atrium line, and at X around 0.2 s where the ventricle line shoots above the dashed aorta line.

Remember valves only respond to pressure differences: the atrioventricular valve shuts when ventricle pressure rises above atrium pressure, and the semilunar valve opens only when ventricle pressure rises above aorta pressure.
walkthrough:
**Read the three pressure lines first**

You have three curves to track. The dotted line is atrium, the solid line is ventricle, the dashed line is aorta. Valves open and close simply because pressure on one side becomes higher than the other.

Rule to hold in mind:
$$valve \ opens \ when \ pressure \ behind > pressure \ in \ front$$

**Work out W and X at the start of ventricular systole**

At W, the ventricle starts to contract so its solid line rises sharply above the low dotted atrium line. Higher pressure below pushes the atrioventricular valve shut, so W is atrioventricular valve closes. A moment later at X, that same rising ventricle line crosses above the falling dashed aorta line. Now ventricle > aorta, so the semilunar valve is forced open and blood is ejected.

**Work out Y and Z at the end of ventricular systole**

At Y around 0.45 s, the solid ventricle line falls steeply below the dashed aorta line. Now aorta > ventricle, so back pressure snaps the semilunar valve shut, giving the little dicrotic notch. At Z, the relaxed ventricle pressure has fallen right down to meet the slowly rising atrium line. When atrium > ventricle, the atrioventricular valve opens and the ventricle fills again.

**Match to the table**

So in order: W closes AV valve, X opens semilunar valve, Y closes semilunar valve, Z opens AV valve. That is exactly row B.

options.A: Reversed at W. W is when ventricle pressure rises above atrium pressure, so the AV valve closes, not opens.
options.B: Perfect match. W closes AV valve, X opens semilunar valve as ventricle exceeds aorta, Y closes semilunar valve as ventricle falls below aorta, Z opens AV valve for filling.
options.C: Mixes up the valves. W and X both involve the ventricle rising above atrium then aorta, so they are AV close then semilunar open, not semilunar open then close.
options.D: Puts semilunar events at the wrong times. The semilunar valve opens at X on the upstroke and closes at Y on the downstroke, not at W and Z.
